newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel barges up on crude, swaps, short-covering.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel barges up on crude, swaps, short-covering.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges closed on the upside on Monday, gaining some $1 on the back of crude and swaps, but traders were mixed over if this strength slipped over into cargoes in the absence of firm bids at higher numbers.
High sulphur barges traded at $87.25 fob Rotterdam and $87.50 fob Antwerp after initial deals at $86.25 to $86.75 fob ARA, compared with Friday's close of $85.50.

"They're higher on crude movement and on (higher) swaps and perceived shortness in the market but I don't think this will hold, I think they will be steady to weaker by the end of the week unless demand comes in," a trader with a major said.
The main players in the market were a trading house that was the seller at the lower set of figures, while an independent oil trade sold at the highest numbers, traders said.
Some said there was short cover buying in the market but others said that sellers were just charging a little more for prompt material.
"There is not too much demand...It is being pushed up by independents, perhaps they are expecting a cargo or covering a shortage, we're not sure," one trader said.
Bunkers rose by some $1, with Rotterdam 380 CST fuel quoted at $89/$90 fob but total ARA business was said to be around 10,000 tonnes only.
Low sulphur barges were traded at $95 fob Rotterdam for 1,200 tonnes picked up by an end-user in Belgium, after the seller cut his asking price $1 for that particular deal.
Other sellers were still heard at $96 while buyers were at $94/$94.

Traders were mixed about high sulphur cargoes, with some saying that they should be notionally higher with barges stronger, but others saying that in the absence of firm bids at higher numbers, the market was steady.
"I personally don't see any buyers out there prepared to bid $83/$84 for cif cargoes," one trader said. "It is very difficult with Russian cargoes coming out and overhanging the market."
A second trader said he heard bid around $82 cif for Russian M-100 cargoes, adding some potential buyers were out there.
"The are asking ridiculously high prices for the Russian stuff," a third trader said.
High sulphur Russian cracked was talked at the two means +$1 for 11 Engler material, which translates into two means minus $2 for lower quality cracked material, one trader said.
"There's the famous $3 missing on Russian cargoes. These people think that these are the values of Russian material but that's why there have not been deals recently," one trader said.

One percent was said to be offered steady with swaps flat to a little higher. Physical talked in the $92/$94 region but some traders said weakness may set into the market with a shut arb to the United States, and no other main outlet seen for a number of cargoes still around.
However, there was unconfirmed talk of a cargo changing hands, and in the absence of price details some traders pegged it to swaps, saying it would be about $93/$93.50 fob.
